system_prompt:
You are an eighth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: A square, with a triangle attached to each side. Each triangle shares a side with the square, shown with a dotted line.]
The shape shown above is cut out of cardboard. The triangle flaps are then folded up along the dotted lines until they touch the edges of the flaps next to them.

Complete the diagram below to show what the shape would look like when viewed from directly above.

[Image: A square.]

Figure, described in words:
Top diagram: A flat net composed of a central square with dashed sides, each side joined to the base of an identical isosceles triangle pointing outward.
Bottom diagram: A square drawn with solid lines, representing the outer border of the shape viewed directly from above, awaiting completion.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Draw the square's outline as the base, then draw the four folded triangle flaps as shapes that meet at the apex of a square-based pyramid. When each triangle is folded up along its dotted side, its apex rises to meet the neighboring flaps, so from directly above the flaps fill the square region and their outer edges form the sides of the square base. Viewed from directly above, the figure shows the original square, with each triangle's sloped faces projecting inward from its four sides meeting at a central point: draw the square, then draw two diagonal lines from each corner of the square to the center, dividing the square into four triangular regions, one per side, and label the center point where the lines meet as the apex of the pyramid.
